class_list_fixed.definition: The name states a quantity, locus, component or relation that the Data Dictionary source text contradicts.

The source text states a qualifier of the quantity — a counting basis, a species basis, a weighting or average, a normalisation, a coordinate convention, a component or a locus — and the name leaves it out.
The stored definition (description or documentation) contradicts the Data Dictionary source text.
The stored name and the stored definition describe different quantities or different scopes, even if each is internally consistent.
The stored unit does not fit the quantity the name states: it is dimensionally wrong for that kind of quantity, or it is the wrong unit for the stated kind of quantity.
The assigned physics domain is not the domain of the quantity the source describes.
The name denotes the same quantity as another live standard name listed for it, so the catalog carries one quantity twice.

plants.label_source: docs/evidence/sn-west-catalog-release/west-name-audit*.md, read row by row by judgment_goldens._west_verdicts

A.rationale: The name specifies 'measurement position', contradicting sources for actuator and hardware locations such as NBI beamlets (nbi/unit/beamlets_group/beamlets/positions/z) and polarizer centre (ece/polarizer/centre/z). Furthermore, the assigned physics domain 'equilibrium' does not fit these diagnostic and heating/actuator coordinates.

B.rationale: The sources' "Vertical (Z) coordinate of position" and unit "m" match the name and definition. However, the positions occur predominantly in diagnostic or device structures such as "reflectometer_fluctuation", "bolometer", "nbi" and "langmuir_probes"; this generic measurement-position coordinate is not specifically an equilibrium quantity, so the assigned domain "equilibrium" is wrong.

A.rationale: Source 3 states the quantity represents electron pressure in the 'post-crash core plasma state', but the stored definition states it is 'in the plasma edge and scrape-off layer'. This contradicts the source text and introduces a disagreement between the locus specified in the name and the locus in the definition.

B.rationale: Source 3 places the named post-crash pressure "in the post-crash core plasma state"; the stored description instead puts it "in the plasma edge and scrape-off layer", contradicting the source and assigning the name a different spatial scope.

A.rationale: The source specifies `ic_antennas/antenna/module/strap/outline/phi` as "Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of outline" within the enclosing structure `strap/outline` ("Strap outline"). The standard name leaves out the locus or component qualifier `outline`, identifying the angle as belonging to the antenna strap rather than its outline.

B.rationale: The source path ends “strap/outline/phi” and states “Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of outline,” with enclosing structure “Strap outline.” The name “toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap” omits this outline-point locus, although the stored definition explicitly supplies it.

A.rationale: The definition states that this quantity 'is the envelope phase, not the carrier oscillation phase.' This contradicts Source 1 ('Phase (φ) measured for a specific interferometer wavelength channel') and Source 2 ('Measured phase of the probing wave relative to its launch phase'), where the measured quantity is the carrier wave phase.

B.rationale: The name leaves out stated qualifiers: Source 1 requires “Phase … for a specific interferometer wavelength channel, corrected for fringe jumps”; Source 2 requires phase “relative to its launch phase”; Source 3 specifies the “envelope” phase “measured relative to the launch phase.”

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, unit, and physics domain consistently describe the vertical coordinate (Z) of a divertor strike point, matching the Data Dictionary sources in both equilibrium constraints and summary boundary parameters.

B.rationale: The sources and stored definition share one quantity: the vertical Z coordinate, in metres, of an individual divertor strike point. Source 1’s measured strike-point array and sources 2–3’s outer/inner points fit the definition’s “one selected strike point, including separately identified inner and outer strike points”; no conflicting scope, unit, or domain is stated.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition consistently specify the vertical (Z) coordinate of the measurement position for an electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostic channel.

B.rationale: The source 'Vertical (Z) coordinate of position' under 'Position of the measurements' and 'ece/channel' denotes an ECE channel’s measurement height; the definition likewise gives the 'Signed vertical coordinate ... measurement position', with matching unit m and ECE diagnostics domain.

A.rationale: The sources, name, and definition describe the detected photoelectron or photon rate (s^-1) per spectral channel or wavelength pixel of a spectrometer channel, with electronic gain compensation and relative calibration applied.

B.rationale: The name’s “spectral_rate” omits the stated counting basis and pixel locus: “photoelectrons per unit time per wavelength pixel.” The definition also conflicts with Source 2: it specifies “photoelectrons” and applies “to each wavelength pixel,” whereas Source 2 states “Detected photon count rate” and “number of photons per unit time recorded by the detector.”

A.rationale: Major radius (radial coordinate) of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard midplane intersection.

B.rationale: The source states "Major radius (R) of the flux surface at the inboard (high-field side) midplane intersection"; the name and stored definition identify that same locus-specific major-radius coordinate. The source unit "m" fits, and the enclosing equilibrium profile structure supports the assigned equilibrium domain.

A.rationale: The source specifies 'apparent_temperature' ('apparent surface temperature from an infrared camera frame'), whereas the name omits the qualifier 'apparent' and the definition contradicts the source by defining it as 'thermodynamic temperature'.

B.rationale: Source: “Processed 2D image of apparent surface temperature”. The name omits “apparent”; the definition instead specifies “thermodynamic temperature” and a “local scalar” at a surface point, contradicting the source’s apparent-temperature 2D image.

A.rationale: Surface area of a diagnostic aperture opening.

B.rationale: The stored scope is “the diagnostic aperture opening” and “distinct from … surface_area_of_detector.” The sources instead include “Surface specification of detector,” “Surface specification of antenna emission,” and reflector documentation “Surface of the object.” Thus the aperture-only name and definition contradict source loci beyond apertures.

A.rationale: The source, stored name, and definitions all specify the minimum safety factor (q value) across the plasma equilibrium.

B.rationale: The source leaf 'q_min/value' is documented as 'Minimum q value' with unit '1'; its parent separately describes 'Minimum q value and position.' The name and stored definition identify the extremal safety-factor value, not its location, and the dimensionless unit and equilibrium domain fit.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition consistently describe the net RF power launched into the vacuum vessel by a lower-hybrid antenna, module, or overall antenna system, with unit W in the auxiliary_heating domain.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is net lower-hybrid launched power: Source 4 says “Net RF power launched from a lower hybrid (LH) antenna into the vacuum vessel,” while Source 7 specifies “the forward power minus the reflected power.” Source 5 covers the system sum. The stored definitions agree; W and auxiliary_heating are appropriate.

A.rationale: Sources 1–19 and the definition specify the field evaluated "at the reference major radius R0". The name leaves out this locus (name_omits_source). Consequently, the name denotes a spatially distributed field while the definition describes only the single-point scalar at the reference radius (name_definition_disagree).

B.rationale: Sources 1–19 specify “at the reference major radius R0”, a locus absent from the name. Source 20 instead says “on GGD grid subsets” and “given on various grid subsets”, contradicting the stored definition’s “at the reference major radius” and documentation’s “component evaluated at the reference radius”.

A.rationale: Polarization ellipticity is defined as the signed minor-to-major semiaxis ratio of the electric-field polarization ellipse, which is a dimensionless ratio. The stored unit 'm' (meters) is dimensionally wrong for an ellipticity.

B.rationale: The definition calls ellipticity “the signed minor-to-major semiaxis ratio,” a dimensionless quantity, yet the stored unit is “m.” The source’s “Initial ellipticity … before entering the plasma” otherwise agrees with the name and stored definition.

A.rationale: The source path pf_passive/loop/element/turns_with_sign and description state the locus as a "passive conductor loop element" ("Each loop is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually"), but the standard name omits the element locus, naming only the passive loop.

B.rationale: The source leaf `pf_passive/loop/element/turns_with_sign` states: “Number of effective turns (with sign) in a passive conductor loop element.” The name omits both the signed basis and the element locus; the enclosing source says loop cross-section elements are “described individually.”

A.rationale: The sources, standard name, and stored definition all describe the Faraday rotation angle induced by passage of a probing beam through magnetized plasma, measured in radians.

B.rationale: Source 2: “Faraday rotation angle induced by passage of the probing beam through the magnetized plasma,” sensitive to “∫n_e·B∥ dl”; the stored definition gives the same accumulated signed rotation. The documentation treats measured and reconstructed values as realizations of one angle. Unit rad and the equilibrium-constraint domain match the sources.

A.rationale: The source specifies the total is "expressed in equivalent electrons", a counting basis omitted by the name. Consequently, the stored name describes a particle or gas count (accumulated_total_gas_count), whereas the stored definition defines an equivalent-electron inventory ($N_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum z_s N_s$), causing name and definition to disagree on the quantity.

B.rationale: The enclosing source states “Accumulated gas injected since plasma breakdown” and a total “expressed in equivalent electrons.” The name accumulated_total_gas_count omits the injection locus, post-breakdown phase, and equivalent-electron counting basis. The stored definition and unit 1 otherwise match the cumulative, species-summed quantity.

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, unit (eV), and domain describe the upper-bound photon energy of a detector channel or emissivity energy band, matching the Data Dictionary sources.

B.rationale: The sources share one quantity: "Upper photon energy bound" of a hard- or soft-X-ray energy band, in eV. The stored definition matches it as the "Upper-bound photon energy" giving the "high-energy cutoff" of an X-ray emission or detection band.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the vertical full height of the rectangular cross-section of a poloidal field coil or element in metres.

B.rationale: The sources state “Vertical full height of the rectangular cross-section”; the definition’s “full vertical extent of the rectangular conductor cross-section of an individual active coil element” describes that same coil-element height. The unit m fits, and magnetic_field_systems is the appropriate domain.

A.rationale: Conversion factor from interferometric phase to line-integrated electron density for an optical line of sight at a given probing wavelength.

B.rationale: The source’s “Conversion factor from measured interferometric phase to line-integrated electron density (∫ne·dl) for a given wavelength channel” matches the stored wavelength-specific phase-to-electron-column-density coefficient along a line of sight; the unit and interferometric diagnostic domain also fit.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the elongation (kappa) of a magnetic flux surface, defined as the ratio of its vertical to radial extent.

B.rationale: Both sources describe flux-surface “Elongation (κ)” as the “ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axes.” The stored extent formula gives that ratio for an elliptical cross-section and defines the same vertical-to-horizontal shape measure per surface. It is dimensionless (unit 1), and the equilibrium profile source supports the assigned domain.

A.rationale: The assigned physics domain is equilibrium, but the sources describe the geometry of hardware components such as "Array of active poloidal field (PF) coils including the central solenoid and shaping coils" (pf_active/coil) and "ic_antennas/antenna/module/strap", which belong to the magnets or heating domains rather than plasma equilibrium.

B.rationale: The source documentation states “Geometric centre R”, but the name only gives a “radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section”; it omits the geometric-centre reference locus. The stored description supplies that locus and otherwise agrees with the source.

A.rationale: Minor radius of the plasma boundary, defined as half the difference between the maximum and minimum major radii of the boundary contour.

B.rationale: The source and stored definition agree on one quantity: “Minor radius (a) of the plasma boundary, defined as (R_max − R_min)/2 of the boundary contour,” matching “half the difference between the maximum and minimum major radii.” The plasma-boundary/LCFS locus, unit m, and equilibrium domain are consistent.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the minimum of the magnetic field magnitude across a magnetic flux surface.

B.rationale: Source: “Minimum magnetic field modulus (|B|_min) on each flux surface as a 1D radial profile in the MHD equilibrium.” The name and definition identify the pointwise minimum of total |B| over a flux surface; the stored unit T and equilibrium domain also match.

A.rationale: Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems excluding Ohmic power.

B.rationale: Source: “Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems (NBI, EC, IC, and LH) excluding Ohmic power.” The name, stored definition, W unit, and auxiliary_heating domain all describe this same whole-plasma aggregate.

A.rationale: The definition states that the quantity is the "measured, signed vertical-field integral" and documentation specifies "that loop's measured value", which directly contradicts Source 1 (`equilibrium/time_slice/constraints/flux_loop/reconstructed`), defined as "Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium".

B.rationale: The description calls this “the measured, signed vertical-field integral,” and the documentation says “that loop's measured value”; Source 1 instead states “Reconstructed value of flux loop” and “Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium.” The name itself is provenance-neutral, and Wb matches the stated flux.

A.rationale: The name is general, but the stored definition restricts scope to "during a disruption" (name_definition_disagree), contradicting Source 1's "primary intrinsic heating channel in tokamak operation" (definition_contradicts_source). Additionally, "total_power" in the name contradicts Source 2, which specifies power dissipated strictly in the "halo region" (name_contradicts_source).

B.rationale: The name omits the source locus “in the plasma.” Source 2 instead states “Ohmic power dissipated in the halo region”, but the documentation integrates over “the full plasma volume” and says this is “rather than denoting only the halo-region contribution”, directly contradicting that source.

A.rationale: Derivative of the volume enclosed by a flux surface with respect to poloidal flux coordinate (dV/dψ).

B.rationale: Source: “Radial derivative of the volume enclosed by a flux surface with respect to poloidal flux (dV/dψ).” The name and definition state this same enclosed-volume derivative; “Wb^-1.m^3” fits m³ per Wb, and the source path places it in equilibrium.

A.rationale: The sources describe the mass flow rate of fluid or coolant passing through a balance-of-plant port, calorimetry component, or cooling loop. The name, definition, kg.s^-1 unit, and assigned physics domain accurately capture this shared quantity without contradiction or omission.

B.rationale: The sources share coolant/fluid mass throughput per unit time: “Mass flow rate (ṁ) of coolant passing through a calorimetry component”, through a cooling loop, or fluid “at a component port”. The stored dm_pass/dt definition matches, and kg.s^-1 and mechanical_measurement_diagnostics fit.

A.rationale: The name, definition, and sources consistently describe the electron temperature evaluated at the magnetic axis, measured in electronvolts within the transport domain.

B.rationale: Both sources state "Electron temperature (Te) at the magnetic axis"; the stored name and definition describe that same local electron kinetic temperature, and the eV unit matches both source units.

A.rationale: Spectral bremsstrahlung photon radiance represents calibrated continuum spectral radiance per unit wavelength, with unit m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1 representing photons per area, second, solid angle, and wavelength.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is continuum bremsstrahlung spectral photon radiance per unit wavelength: source 2 calls it "continuum spectral radiance measured at the centre" "per unit wavelength." The stored photon-rate definition, central-wavelength evaluation, and m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1 unit consistently describe that quantity.

A.rationale: Toroidal angle of the projection of a toroidal field (B_φ) probe's normal vector onto the horizontal plane, measured counter-clockwise from the outward major radius direction.

B.rationale: Source and stored definition both describe “the projection of a toroidal field (B_φ) probe's normal vector onto the horizontal plane,” measured from outward R, with values “modulo pi” in “(-pi/2,pi/2]”. The name identifies the same probe-specific toroidal angle; rad and magnetic_field_diagnostics are appropriate.

A.rationale: The standard name, stored definition, and Data Dictionary sources all describe the lower bound or minimum threshold of photon energy for an energy band or detector channel/pixel.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is the lower photon-energy edge of an X-ray band: the sources call it the “Lower bound of the energy band” or the pixel threshold where “photons are counted only if their energy is above this value.” The documentation covers both “detection or emission band,” and eV is an energy unit.

A.rationale: normalized poloidal flux coordinate

B.rationale: Stored documentation: “The coordinate is the square-root form, ρ_pol,norm = √ψ_N.” Source 18 instead identifies “Normalised poloidal flux coordinate (ψ_norm)” and says “the flux being normalized” from axis to separatrix; that is the linear normalized flux ψ_N, not its square root.

A.rationale: The source, name, and stored definition all describe the loop voltage at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface), with unit V representing the toroidal electromotive force driving ohmic current.

B.rationale: The sources describe “Loop voltage ... at the last closed flux surface (LCFS), the inductive EMF driving ohmic current”; the name and definition describe that same boundary loop voltage, with the appropriate unit V.

A.rationale: The source, standard name, and stored definition all describe the flux-surface average of the inverse square of the magnetic field magnitude, with consistent units of T^-2 and assigned domain equilibrium.

B.rationale: Source: “Flux surface averaged inverse square of the total magnetic field, ⟨1/B²⟩ (gm4), as a radial profile.” The name and definition identify that same average of B⁻² for the total equilibrium field magnitude; source and stored unit are both “T^-2”, and the enclosing equilibrium structure supports the assigned domain.

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, and source text all consistently describe the flux-surface-averaged major radius \langle R \rangle in meters as an equilibrium profile metric coefficient.

B.rationale: The source states “Flux surface averaged major radius (gm8 = 〈R〉)” and “Represents the mean major radius over a flux surface”; the name and stored definition identify that same averaged radius, with the appropriate unit “m” and physics domain “equilibrium”.

A.rationale: The source specifies the locus as an "ICRH antenna module" within enclosing structure "ic_antennas/antenna/module" ("Set of antenna modules"), but the standard name omits the module locus, naming only the overall "ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna".

B.rationale: The source states “Phase of the forward power wave for an ICRH antenna module, measured relative to the first module,” and the enclosing locus is “Set of antenna modules.” The name only says “forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna,” omitting the module locus and the first-module relative-phase reference.

A.rationale: The standard name and definition specify a limiter tile, but the source text establishes the component as a limiter unit (wall/description_2d/limiter/unit: 'Set of limiter units') representing the 'limiting surface', not a tile.

B.rationale: Source “Vertical (Z) coordinate of outline” with unit “m”, under “Irregular outline of the limiting surface” and “Set of limiter units”, matches the stored “Signed vertical (Z) coordinate of each point on a limiter-tile boundary contour”; structural_components fits this limiter geometry quantity.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the change in the vacuum toroidal magnetic field product with major radius, known as the vacuum poloidal current function, relative to its initial value at the start of plasma.

B.rationale: The source’s “Change in the vacuum toroidal field product … from the start of plasma” matches the stored “ΔF_vac=F_vac−F_vac,initial=R B_φ,vac−R B_φ,vac,initial”: one signed change in vacuum field times major radius. The unit T.m and domain magnetic_field_systems fit.

A.rationale: The source specifies the 'decay of electron temperature (Te)' and 'Exponential decay time constant', but the name states 'electron_decay_time' without temperature and without specifying exponential decay (distinguishing it from linear), creating a contradiction and disagreement with the source and stored definition.

B.rationale: The source’s “Exponential decay time constant (τ) characterizing the decay of electron temperature (Te) at the magnetic axis during a disruption” matches the stored “Exponential e-folding time of the electron temperature at the magnetic axis during a disruption”; seconds fit this time constant.

A.rationale: The name specifies generic 'power', while the definition restricts the quantity specifically to 'Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state', representing different scopes and quantities.

B.rationale: Name and definition both denote "Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state, integrated over the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface." W fits power, auxiliary_heating fits wave-energy absorption, and no other live names are supplied for duplicate comparison.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition share the poloidal component of the momentum source for a specific neutral state, represented on GGD grid elements with the Data Dictionary's documented area-normalized unit kg.m^-1.s^-2.

B.rationale: The source specifies “a neutral species charge state” and “different charge states of the species,” plus “momentum source density.” The name omits the charge-state and density qualifiers, while the stored definition instead says “one specified internal state,” changing the state basis.

A.rationale: Real part of the right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field component along a beam or ray path.

B.rationale: Source 1 calls it the “Real part of the right-hand circularly polarized electric field component (E−) along the beam/ray path”; Source 2 and the enclosing structure repeat that path locus. The name omits the beam/ray-path qualifier. The real-part definition, V.m^-1 unit, and electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics domain otherwise fit.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the thermal power or heat deposited in the breeder blanket breeding zone, measured in watts within the plant systems domain.

B.rationale: The source says “Thermal power directed toward the tritium breeding blanket module,” but the name omits that module locus. Stored documentation instead specifies “blanket-level heat input” and “aggregates heat deposition at the blanket level,” contradicting the source’s module scope. W and plant_systems otherwise fit the heat-deposition rate.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition all describe the line-averaged tungsten ion number density along a chord.

B.rationale: The enclosing source specifies “line-averaged ion density (ni) per ion species”; the name omits that ion basis, while the definition states “Number density of tungsten ions” and “excluding neutral tungsten atoms.”

A.rationale: The source path calorimetry/group/component/transit_time and description define the transit time "to travel from the inlet to the outlet of a calorimetry component", but the name assigns the locus to a "plant_component_port", contradicting the source component locus.

B.rationale: The source’s “Transit time for coolant to travel from the inlet to the outlet of a calorimetry component” and the stored “Elapsed time for coolant to traverse the associated plant component from inlet to outlet” describe the same single-component coolant travel duration; the unit “s” fits that time quantity.

A.rationale: The source text, standard name, and definition all describe the normalized plasma internal inductance li_3, defined as 2/(R0·μ0²·Ip²) ∫ Bp² dV, with dimensionless unit 1 in the equilibrium physics domain.

B.rationale: The sources specify “The li_3 definition is used” and the “ITER normalization convention”, but “normalized_plasma_internal_inductance” states only generic normalization and omits the particular li_3 convention.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition share the concept of resistive poloidal magnetic flux losses accumulated over time from discharge start (psi_res), measured in Wb.

B.rationale: Source defines ψ_res as the “time-integrated volume-averaged product of toroidal electric field and ohmic current density normalised by the plasma current”; the name conveys cumulative resistive poloidal-flux loss but omits the volume averaging and plasma-current normalisation. Wb and the stored definition otherwise agree.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition all consistently specify the dimensionless tritium breeding ratio of an individual breeding blanket module, defined as tritium atoms produced per fusion neutron.

B.rationale: Source calls it “Tritium breeding ratio (TBR) of a breeding blanket module” and “A key figure of merit for tritium self-sufficiency and blanket performance”; this breeding-performance quantity is not a structural component, so `structural_components` is wrong. The module locus, per-fusion-neutron basis and unit `1` otherwise agree.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition share the electrical power consumed by an individual plant subsystem during fusion plant operation, measured in watts.

B.rationale: The source specifies 'Electrical power consumed by an individual subsystem' within 'Electric plant operation'; 'power_of_plant_subsystem' omits that electric-plant-operation locus and the electrical-consumption qualifier.

A.rationale: All sources, the standard name, and the definition describe the local electron number density ($n_e$), representing the number of electrons per unit physical volume, consistently with the unit m^-3.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is electron number density: 'The local density is the differential electron count per physical volume,' so m^-3 fits. 'Equilibrium' is not the source domain overall: sources say 'measured via Stark broadening,' 'measured at an embedded Langmuir probe position,' and 'reconstructed from reflectometer measurements.'

A.rationale: The source path and documentation describe a full-wave code solution for coherent wave propagation driving ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH), which belongs to the heating and current drive domain, not electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics.

B.rationale: The source’s “Right-hand circularly polarised component (E−) … perpendicular to the static magnetic field” matches the stored “Complex E-minus contribution … transverse to the static magnetic field.” V.m^-1 is the appropriate electric-field unit, and electromagnetic_wave_diagnostics fits the coherent-wave source.

A.rationale: Major-radius coordinate of a geometric reference point defining the poloidal field coil cross section.

B.rationale: The sources specify distinct loci: “Major radius (R) coordinate of first point,” “of second point,” and the annulus “Centre major radius.” The name omits the reference-point locus, leaving one generic coil radial coordinate for different point locations.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the cross-sectional area of a turn of a toroidal magnetic field probe coil, with consistent units and domain.

B.rationale: Source: “Physical cross-sectional area of a single turn … Multiplied by the number of turns, yields the effective area”; the stored definition likewise excludes turn multiplication, but the name states only “area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe”, omitting the single-turn counting basis.

A.rationale: Minimum pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver.

B.rationale: The source fixes the locus: “Minimum volumetric flow rate of a gas injection valve,” reinforced by enclosing `gas_injection/valve`. `minimum_gas_flow` omits that valve/injection-system locus. The shared `Pa.m^3.s^-1` unit and “lower operational bound” otherwise agree with the stored pressure-volume throughput and minimum-limit definition.

A.rationale: The source, name, and stored definition all describe the initial velocity of the pellet at entry into the vacuum chamber, with matching units in m.s^-1 and correct assignment to the fueling domain.

B.rationale: Source: "Initial speed of a pellet as it enters the vacuum chamber." The name instead states velocity and omits the vacuum-chamber-entry locus. Stored documentation defines a center-of-mass vector whose radial, toroidal and vertical velocities are "its components"; this contradicts the source's scalar entry speed.

A.rationale: Pressure-volume gas flow rate at the exit of an injection valve.

B.rationale: Both sources state “Flow rate at the exit of the valve”; Source 2 also says “at the exit of an injection valve.” The name gas_flow_of_valve identifies valve gas flow but omits the source-stated exit locus.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition all describe the detected neutron count rate (event rate) registered by a neutron detector.

B.rationale: The source specifies “Detected neutron count rate … for a neutron detector channel operating in pulse counting mode” and “Detected counts per second.” The name omits the pulse-counting-mode qualifier; the stored detector-event rate and s^-1 unit otherwise fit.

A.rationale: The source, definition, and name all describe the cumulative hydrogen atom inventory (in equivalent electrons) delivered by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase.

B.rationale: The enclosing source states that these accumulated prefill quantities are “expressed in equivalent electrons,” a counting basis absent from accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count. The stored definition’s “Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory” agrees with the source, and unit 1 is appropriate.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition agree on the vertical (Z) component of force density (volumetric force), with matching unit N.m^-3 and structural_components domain.

B.rationale: The leaf says 'Vertical (Z) coordinate of em force density,' and the enclosing source specifies 'wall' and 'Electromagnetic force density computed by the cross-product of j_total x b_field.' The name vertical_volumetric_force gives only the vertical force-density component, omitting the electromagnetic basis and wall locus.

A.rationale: Position of the detector aperture outline vertices along the first local-tangential axis in the detector local coordinate system.

B.rationale: Source 1 says “Positions of the detector aperture outline vertices along the x1 axis”; Source 2 likewise says “detector/aperture outline vertices”. The name ends at “coordinate_of_detector”, omitting the aperture-outline-vertex locus. The stored definition’s “detector-outline vertex” confirms that locus; m and spectroscopy otherwise fit.

A.rationale: Vertical (Z) coordinate of the bolometer detector center.

B.rationale: Source “detector/centre/z” is the “Vertical (Z) coordinate of centre”, but the name omits the detector-centre locus. The definition’s “center of a bolometer detector” also overstates the source: for geometry_type=1 or 3, centre is the local-system origin, merely “located within the detector/aperture area”.

A.rationale: atomic fraction of a constituent species in the SPI propellant or fragmentation working fluid

B.rationale: The sources specify distinct loci, "fragmentation gas mixture" and "propellant gas composition"; the name's generic "working fluid" omits which gas mixture the atomic fraction describes.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition all consistently describe the normalized linear growth rate of a gyrokinetic eigenmode for a given wavevector in local flux-tube geometry.

B.rationale: The source qualifies the rate as “for a given wavevector in the local flux-tube geometry.” The name includes linear, normalized and gyrokinetic eigenmode, but omits both the specified-wavevector and local-flux-tube scope; the stored definition expressly includes “at a specified wavevector … in the local flux-tube approximation.”

A.rationale: The sources, standard name, and stored definition all describe the relative molecular fraction of a gas species within an injected gas mixture.

B.rationale: Every source documents “Relative fraction of this species (in molecules) in the gas mixture.” The live name neutral_species_fraction denotes that same per-species injected-gas fraction, so molecular_fraction duplicates it; the stored definition and dimensionless unit otherwise agree.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition consistently describe the propellant gas flow rate (pressure-volume throughput in Pa.m^3.s^-1) delivered at the exit of a pellet injector gas supply.

B.rationale: The source specifies “Gas flow rate at the exit of the … propellant gas supply,” but “gas_flow_of_pellet_injector” omits the supply-exit locus. The stored pressure–volume throughput definition and Pa.m^3.s^-1 unit otherwise agree with the source.

A.rationale: The source texts, name, and definition consistently specify the scalar or isotropic pressure of suprathermal (fast) particles on magnetically trapped orbits.

prompts.system:
You are an independent physics auditor of the standard names of a fusion data dictionary. A standard name identifies exactly one quantity. You are given one name record at a time and must decide which of these fixed defect classes apply to it:

- `name_contradicts_source`: The name states a quantity, locus, component or relation that the Data Dictionary source text contradicts.
- `name_omits_source`: The source text states a qualifier of the quantity — a counting basis, a species basis, a weighting or average, a normalisation, a coordinate convention, a component or a locus — and the name leaves it out.
- `definition_contradicts_source`: The stored definition (description or documentation) contradicts the Data Dictionary source text.
- `name_definition_disagree`: The stored name and the stored definition describe different quantities or different scopes, even if each is internally consistent.
- `unit_wrong`: The stored unit does not fit the quantity the name states: it is dimensionally wrong for that kind of quantity, or it is the wrong unit for the stated kind of quantity.
- `wrong_physics_domain`: The assigned physics domain is not the domain of the quantity the source describes.
- `duplicate_of_live_name`: The name denotes the same quantity as another live standard name listed for it, so the catalog carries one quantity twice.

Rules:
- Report every class that applies. A name may carry more than one.
- Report an empty list when no class applies. Do not invent a defect, and do not flag a name for style, brevity, missing prose, or for information no part of the record states.

Standard name: accumulated_tritium_prefill_count
Definition (stored description): Tritium prefill count is the amount of tritium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown, expressed as one equivalent electron per tritium atom.
Documentation (stored): Tritium prefill count is the accumulated amount of neutral tritium introduced by gas injection during prefill before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each tritium atom contributes one equivalent electron; a neutral diatomic tritium molecule contributes two. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}(t)\,dt $$ where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the tritium equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the accumulated count of injected tritium atoms including molecular constituents, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is their introduction rate, $t$ is time, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time. This quantity counts injected tritium, not the retained or ionized tritium inventory. It excludes post-breakdown gas injection, wall recycling, neutral-beam fueling, and pellet fueling. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not an actual free-electron count. It is the tritium contribution to the [total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count), which sums over all injected species. The [accumulated tritium count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection) instead counts tritium introduced after plasma breakdown.
